concerns.text: FR-001 states that the dataset includes 'human‑annotated feasibility scores' that are generated via a deterministic antonym‑lookup/synthetic labeling procedure. Because the same lexical resources and rule‑based logic are also used by the symbolic constraint‑graph parser (FR-002), the validation target (human scores) is not independent of the predictor, creating a circular/tautological validation.

FR-003 requires the baseline verifier to be evaluated against the same synthetic feasibility scores described in FR-001. Since those scores are derived from the same rule‑based system that produces the graphs, the baseline alignment metric is not an external ground truth.

FR-005 specifies a paired t‑test/Wilcoxon test comparing baseline and graph‑augmented alignment scores relative to the synthetic human_score. Because the human_score is deterministically derived from the same rule‑based resources as the graph construction, the statistical test does not assess genuine improvement against an independent reality.

The assumption that a synthetic 'degree of partial compliance' metric can serve as a valid proxy for true human feasibility is questionable. Without collecting real human judgments (e.g., via crowd‑sourced rating of edit plausibility), the study cannot demonstrate that the graph‑augmented verifier aligns better with actual human perception.
